findings.title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler cannot be instantiated
findings.body: MetricAlertDetectorHandler is now an empty `pass` body inheriting from StatefulDetectorHandler, but StatefulDetectorHandler declares `build_occurrence_and_event_data` as an @abc.abstractmethod (newly added in this PR). Because GroupType.detector_handler = MetricAlertDetectorHandler, the `detector_handler` property on the Detector model does `group_type.detector_handler(self)` and will raise `TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class MetricAlertDetectorHandler with abstract method build_occurrence_and_event_data` (along with `counter_names`, `get_dedupe_value`, and `get_group_key_values`, which are also unimplemented). This is a regression introduced by adding the abstract hook without providing any concrete implementation for the only concrete subclass in the codebase.

findings.title: evaluate docstring still describes list return
findings.body: The PR changed `StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate` to return `dict[DetectorGroupKey, DetectorEvaluationResult]` but the docstring still reads: 'Evaluates a given data packet and returns a list of `DetectorEvaluationResult`. There will be one result for each group key result in the packet, unless the evaluation is skipped due to various rules.' Update the wording to describe the dict keyed by `DetectorGroupKey` so consumers reading the abstract method's contract aren't misled.

findings.title: PriorityLevel(new_status) relies on enum values matching across modules
findings.body: `evaluate_group_key_value` computes `new_status: DetectorPriorityLevel` and then calls `self.build_occurrence_and_event_data(group_key, value, PriorityLevel(new_status))`, converting a `sentry.workflow_engine.types.DetectorPriorityLevel` member into a `sentry.types.group.PriorityLevel` member. These are two distinct enums imported from different modules; if their integer values ever diverge, `PriorityLevel(...)` will raise `ValueError` at runtime, breaking all stateful detectors whenever a non-OK status fires. Either pass the detector-side enum directly through the hook (and let implementers convert), or assert a mapping in tests, so the conversion is explicit rather than relying on coincidental value parity.

findings.title: test_state_results_multi_group uses wrong value for group_2
findings.body: In `test_state_results_multi_group` the data packet is `{'dedupe': 2, 'group_vals': {'group_1': 6, 'group_2': 10}}`, but the second occurrence is built with `build_mock_occurrence_and_event(detector.detector_handler, 'group_2', 6, PriorityLevel.HIGH)` — i.e. value=6 instead of 10. The test still passes because `build_mock_occurrence_and_event` ignores `value`, so it never validates that `build_occurrence_and_event_data` receives the per-group value. Use the correct 10 (or assert that the recorded mock was called with the correct value) so a regression that swaps or drops the value would be caught.
